newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar and the currency basket on Monday after the U.S. currency surged in Europe against the yen, dealers said.

"The day opened with a sharp jump of the dollar following its rise abroad. When the dollar reached 3.3820 shekels investors used the opportunity to sell dollars and the shekel recovered mildly," said Zahi Eleas, a dealer at Bank Leumi.
"The basket traded today at the bottom (of its trading band) and the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market, buying dollars on a relatively low scale," Elias added.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3810 shekels against 3.3610 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6651 shekels against 3.6636 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6982 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7166 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9856 shekels after 2.0087 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3800 shekels.
